title: Automated LTS release coordinator and progressive traffic tapering for Hosted API
creator: Ana Rodrigues
description:
Problem: Hosted API upgrades currently rely on manual orchestration across regions and model variants. We lack a canonical LTS channel workflow with automated tapering of traffic and explicit gates tied to SLOs and quality checks. This leads to irregular rollout cadence, variable blast radius, and slow emergency rollbacks.

Proposal: Build an "Automated LTS Release Coordinator" service + operator that: (1) publishes release artifacts to a release registry with LTS/stable/edge labels, (2) orchestrates progressive traffic tapering across regions and capacity tiers, (3) evaluates gating signals (error budget, p50/p95 latency, model-quality regressions) and automatically pauses/rolls back if thresholds breach, and (4) exposes a runbook + audit trail for compliance. The coordinator will integrate with existing routing layer (safety mesh), runtime health metrics, and console dashboards.

Scope: Hosted API control plane and routing rules for traffic shifts, release registry metadata (version/LTS tag/compatibility matrix), gating evaluation engine, operator for automated shifts and emergency rollback, observability dashboard updates, and a plain-text runbook for on-call. No database schema changes in this ticket.

Trade-offs considered: fully managed blue/green is fastest to implement but expensive (duplicate capacity). Progressive tapering reduces cost but requires stricter observability. We opted for a hybrid: maintain lightweight shadow deployments for the first 10% of traffic in critical regions, then progressive taper with automatic gating.

Non-goals: Dedicated capacity private deployments (handled in a separate Private Release flow), model content-level evaluation (handled by Optimize team evals).
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can publish a release with LTS or stable tags and store metadata in release-registry
Coordinator can execute a traffic taper plan: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% configurable per-region
Gating thresholds (error-rate, p95 latency, quality-regression) are configurable and enforced automatically
Rollback path triggers within 2 minutes of gate breach and reverts traffic to last healthy version
Audit log entries emitted for each step (publish, shift, gate-evaluation, rollback) and visible in Console
E2E smoke tests (staging) exercising the taper and rollback pass in CI
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dry run (staging): deploy coordinator to staging and publish test LTS tag; run the taper plan with synthetic traffic and validate metrics collection (1 day)
Phase 1 - Canary regional pilot (us-west-2): 0%->5%->25% over 2h with 30m observation windows; gate thresholds conservative (tight) (2 days)
Phase 2 - Cross-region slow roll: add eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 with 12h between region starts; thresholds relaxed once healthy (3 days)
Phase 3 - LTS publish + full global roll: update release-registry tag to LTS and execute 60%->100% steps with extended monitoring (24h), followed by post-rollout QA
Phase 4 - Postmortem and adjustments: collect metrics, update thresholds, and write follow-ups (1 week)
Manual override: on-call can pause or force rollback via Console button with two-person approval (SRE + PM)
rollback_plan: Automatic: If any gate reports breach (error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency increase > 30% OR model-quality regression > configured delta), coordinator triggers rollback to previous version and ramps traffic back over 5 minutes
Semi-automatic: If transient degradation detected, coordinator pauses further taper steps and notifies SRE + PM with diagnostics dump
Manual: On-call runs 'coordinator rollback <release>' or uses Console UI; runbook steps documented in Confluence (link below)
Post-rollback: Create incident ticket, attach coordinator audit trail, and run postmortem within 72h
